title: 吗: yes-no questions
summary: Lets you turn any statement into a yes-no question by adding 吗 at the end, as in 你是老师吗？
structure: Subject + 不 + Verb (+ Object) + 吗？
explanation:
吗 is a little word that turns a statement into a yes-no question. 你是老师。 means "You are a teacher." Add 吗 at the end and you get 你是老师吗？ "Are you a teacher?"

You don't change the word order at all. Just keep the sentence as it is and put 吗 right at the end, before the question mark. This works with any verb: 你喝茶吗？ "Do you drink tea?" or 你有手机吗？ "Do you have a phone?"

Chinese has no single word for "yes" or "no". To answer, repeat the verb: 是 / 不是, 喝 / 不喝, 有 / 没有. So for 你喜欢狗吗？ you answer 喜欢 or 不喜欢, not 是.

Don't put 吗 in a question that already has a question word like 什么, 谁 or 哪儿 (你喝什么？ is already a question). Also don't add it to A不A questions like 你是不是老师？. These questions already work on their own. And don't mix up 吗 with 呢: 呢 asks "and you?" or "what about…?", while 吗 asks for a yes or a no.

examples.en: Do you have a mobile phone?

examples.zh: 你今天晚上想看电影吗？
examples.en: Do you want to see a movie tonight?

mistakes.why: 什么 already makes this a question, so you don't add 吗. Use 吗 only to turn a statement into a yes-no question.
是不是 (the A不A form) is already a question. Use either 你是不是老师？ or 你是老师吗？, but not both together.
吗 always goes at the very end of the sentence, never at the start or in the middle.

why: Correct: adding 吗 at the end turns the statement into a yes-no question.
呢 asks "and you?" or "what about…?", not a plain yes-no question. Use 吗 here.
什么 means "what" and must stand where the unknown thing is. It can't be tacked onto the end of a statement to ask yes or no.
Correct: 你喜欢喝茶 is a normal statement, so adding 吗 makes a yes-no question.
什么 already makes a question, so it can't be used together with 吗.
喝不喝 (the A不A form) is already a question, so it can't be used together with 吗.
Correct: the statement stays as it is, and 吗 goes at the end.
Nothing comes after 吗. It must be the last word of the question.
吗 can't start a sentence. It always goes at the end.
是不是 already makes a question, so you can't add 吗 as well.

exercises.prompt: Which means "Does she work at a hospital?"
why: Correct: a full statement plus 吗 at the end makes a yes-no question.
呢 doesn't make a yes-no question. Use 吗 to ask for a yes or a no.
哪儿 already asks "where", so 吗 can't be added. The sentence also doesn't mean "at a hospital".
吗 can't go in the middle of the sentence. Put it at the end.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you 你喜欢狗吗？ Which is a natural "yes" answer?
why: Correct: to say yes, repeat the verb from the question, here 喜欢.
是 is not a general "yes". Use it only when the question has 是 in it.
有 means "have", and the question didn't use 有. Repeat the verb 喜欢 instead.

exercises.instruction: Turn it into a 吗 question.
why: Correct: keep the statement as it is and add 吗 at the end.
吗 doesn't go after the subject. It goes at the very end of the sentence.
呢 doesn't make a yes-no question. Use 吗.
什么 already makes a question, so it can't be used with 吗.

exercises.instruction: Turn it into a 吗 question.
why: Correct: 吗 works with negative sentences too. Just add it at the end: "Aren't you working today?"
不 must stay before the verb 上班. Don't move it. Only add 吗 at the end.
吗 can't go in the middle of the sentence. It goes at the end.

exercises.why: Keep the normal statement order (subject + verb + object) and put 吗 at the end.
The statement 这是你的手机 stays in its normal order, and 吗 comes last.

exercises.en: Are you going to the supermarket tomorrow?
exercises.why: Time words like 明天 can go before or after the subject, but 吗 always stays at the end.
